q: What does a vision-capable chat model return after it reads an image in a prompt?
opts: A text answer about the image
Always a JSON list of bounding boxes
exp: Vision-capable chat models take images as input and respond in text, such as a description or an answer to a question. Creating images needs an image-generation model, audio output needs an audio-capable model, and structured boxes come from vision services such as object detection.

ctx: A software support bot lets users upload screenshots of error dialogs. Each reply should state the error code and suggest a fix.
q: Which approach fits?
opts: Key phrase extraction on the screenshot's file name
Send the screenshot to a vision-capable model with instructions to read the error code and suggest a fix
exp: A vision-capable model can read the text in the screenshot and, guided by instructions, explain the error and suggest steps. File names do not contain the error, speech synthesis creates audio, and image generation creates pictures instead of reading them.

q: For each of the following statements about images in prompts, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: A request holds one image, so a photo and a reference image need separate requests.
Image inputs add nothing to the token usage of a request.
Images must be converted to text with OCR before any vision-capable model can use them.
exp: No for the first: several images can be sent together and compared. No for the second: images are converted into tokens, which affects usage and cost. No for the third: vision-capable models read images directly.

q: Complete the sentences about sending images to a vision-capable model.
tpl: An image can be sent by {0} or as base64-encoded data. The model then answers in {1}.
exp: Images are referenced by URL or embedded as base64 data in the request, and the model replies with text. Phone calls and faxes are not ways to send images to an API, and these models do not answer in video or Morse code.

q: Which statement about prompts for image generation is true?
opts: Vague prompts give the most predictable results
Describing the subject, style and composition usually improves the result
Prompts must be shorter than three words
exp: Specific prompts that describe what to show, in what style and how it is arranged guide the model toward the intended image. Vague prompts give unpredictable results, and there are no rules limiting prompts to three words or forbidding colors.

q: A real estate website wants to show empty rooms with furniture added. Which approach fits, and what should the site do?
opts: Use OCR on the room photos
Use image editing to add furniture to the photos, and note that the images are virtually staged
exp: Image editing can add content to an existing photo, and labeling the result as virtually staged keeps buyers informed, which supports transparency. OCR reads text, classification labels images, and speech to text works on audio, so none of them add furniture.

q: Match each requirement to the image-generation setting that fits it. Each setting can be used once or not at all.
items: Ten rough logo ideas, created quickly
One final, high-detail product image
A logo with no background
targets: Low quality setting with several images
exp: Quick drafts suit a low quality setting with several images per request, a final hero image suits high quality, and a logo without background needs the transparent background option. Speech synthesis creates audio and has nothing to do with image generation.

q: Which TWO are responsible practices for a public image-generation feature? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: Allow realistic images of real people doing things they never did
Keep content filters on and handle blocked prompts gracefully
Hide that the images are generated by AI
Preserve the Content Credentials on generated images
exp: Content filters block harmful requests, and Content Credentials let viewers see that images were AI-generated. Fake realistic images of real people, hiding AI generation and ignoring abuse all increase the risk of harm.

q: In Image Analysis, what is a visual feature?
opts: A type of analysis that you request, such as TAGS or READ
exp: Visual features are the kinds of analysis you ask for, such as CAPTION, TAGS, OBJECTS, PEOPLE, READ or SMART_CROPS, and the result contains a section for each one. They are not display settings or deployments.

q: A recycling app must sort photos of items into exactly one of four categories: Plastic, Glass, Metal or Paper. Which approach gives a consistent answer from that list?
opts: Send the photo to a multimodal model with structured output that allows only the four categories
exp: A multimodal model can judge the material, and a structured output schema that lists only the four allowed values keeps every answer in the expected set. OCR reads text, speech to text works on audio, and smart crops only suggests thumbnails.

q: For each of the following statements about Image Analysis, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Dense captions give one longer caption for the whole image.
Smart crops can create new image content.
Image Analysis reads text in many languages.
exp: No for the first: dense captions return a caption for each of several regions. No for the second: smart crops only suggests regions of the existing image; it does not create content. Yes for the third: the Read feature supports many languages and scripts.

q: Put the steps of an alt-text feature that uses Image Analysis in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: Check the caption's confidence score
Generate a new image
Upload or select the image
Use the caption as alt text, or flag it for review if the confidence is low
Call Image Analysis with the CAPTION feature
exp: The image is selected, analyzed with CAPTION, the caption's confidence is checked, and the caption is then used or sent for review. Generating a new image would replace the content instead of describing it.

q: Which value in a Content Understanding result shows how sure the service is about a field's value?
exp: Each field can include a confidence score from 0 to 1, which apps use to decide whether a person should review the value. Page counts, file names and API versions say nothing about how reliable a value is.

q: An expense app receives receipts written in several languages. How should you handle them with Content Understanding?
opts: Create a separate Azure tenant for each language
Have staff translate every receipt by hand first
Use one analyzer schema with clear field descriptions, because the service can read many languages
exp: Content extraction reads text in many languages, and generative field extraction fills the same fields regardless of the receipt's language, guided by clear descriptions. Separate tenants and manual translation add cost without benefit, and speech synthesis does not read receipts.

q: Match each receipt field to the type that fits it. Each type can be used once or not at all.
items: total_amount
purchase_date
store_name
items_purchased
exp: An amount is a number, a purchase date is a date, a store name is a string, and a list of items with their details is an array of objects. None of these fields is a simple true or false value, so boolean is not used.

q: For each of the following statements about Content Understanding, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Content Understanding returns a document's content as Markdown.
You must write your own OCR code before using Content Understanding.
A field schema can include text, number and date fields.
exp: Yes for the first: the extracted content is returned as Markdown, which is useful for search and RAG. No for the second: content extraction, including OCR, is built into the service. Yes for the third: schemas support several field types.

q: An image analyzer needs a field named photo_description that holds a sentence about what the image shows. Which method should it use?
exp: A description is created from the image, so the field uses generate. Extract is for values printed in documents, classify picks one value from a fixed list, and delete is not a field method.

ctx: A car rental company photographs each car when it is returned. It needs a field damage_present with the value Yes or No and a field damage_notes with a short text description.
q: Which field methods should the analyzer use?
opts: No fields; staff should write the notes by hand
Classify for damage_present and generate for damage_notes
exp: Yes or No is a fixed set of values, so classify fits damage_present, while the notes are free text created from the photo, so generate fits damage_notes. Extract is supported only for documents, translate is not a field method, and manual notes defeat the purpose.

q: Complete the sentences about image analyzer fields.
tpl: A field whose value must be Red, Blue or Green uses the {0} method. A field that lists every text label visible on a product uses the {1} method.
exp: A fixed set of colors calls for classify. A list of visible labels is open-ended, so the generate method produces it from the image. Extract is supported only for documents, and translate is not a field method.

q: Which TWO statements about Content Understanding image analyzers are true? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
opts: They always return a fixed tag list that you cannot change
You define the fields that they return
Their fields are filled by generative models that follow your field descriptions
They work only on PDF files
exp: Image analyzers are schema-driven: you choose the fields, and generative models fill them using your descriptions. They do not return a fixed tag list, they do not need audio, and they process images rather than only PDFs.

q: Which input does a Content Understanding audio analyzer process?
opts: Audio files, such as WAV or MP3 recordings
exp: Audio analyzers take recordings, transcribe them and produce fields from the transcript. Photos go to image analyzers, and spreadsheets and fonts are not audio input.

ctx: HR records exit interviews. For each recording it wants the main reason for leaving, as one of Pay, Manager, Growth or Other, and a short summary.
q: Which analyzer design fits?
opts: An audio analyzer with a classify field for the reason and a generate field for the summary
exp: The interviews are audio, so an audio analyzer transcribes them; a classify field keeps the reason within the four categories, and a generate field writes the summary. Image analyzers, OCR and text to speech do not analyze spoken interviews.

q: For each of the following statements about audio and video analyzers, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Audio analyzers produce a summary without creating a transcript of the recording.
Video analyzers support results for every segment of a video.
Video analyzers ignore the audio track completely.
exp: No for the first: transcription is the starting point of audio analysis, and generated fields such as summaries are based on it. Yes for the second: fields can be generated per segment. No for the third: video analysis uses both the frames and the transcribed audio.

q: Match each need when analyzing a recorded webinar to the output that provides it. Each output can be used once or not at all.
items: When each scene starts and ends
Who spoke and what they said
A one-sentence summary of each scene
The text shown on the slides
targets: A generated field for each segment
exp: Segmentation gives start and end times, the transcript with speaker labels shows who said what, a generated per-segment field summarizes each scene, and OCR on keyframes reads slide text. Smart crops is an image thumbnail feature and does not answer any of these needs.

q: Why might a team use Content Understanding instead of writing its own OCR and parsing code?
opts: It is the only way to read text from files
It handles reading, structure and field extraction for many formats, with confidence scores and grounding
It removes the need to write any code at all
exp: The service combines content extraction, layout, field extraction, confidence scores and grounding across documents, images, audio and video, which would take a lot of effort to build yourself. Other ways to read text exist, apps still call it from code, and it does not shorten documents.

q: An app needs to analyze an invoice that is stored in Azure Blob Storage. What should it send to Content Understanding?
opts: An email with the invoice attached
A printed copy of the invoice
An audio version of the invoice
The file's URL, for example with a SAS token, or the file bytes, to the analyze operation
exp: The analyze operation accepts the content either as a URL that the service can read or as the file data in the request. Email, printed copies and audio versions are not ways to submit a file to the API.

q: Complete the sentence about reading Content Understanding results.
tpl: After starting the analysis, the app polls until the status is {0}, and then reads the {1} from the result.
exp: The long-running operation reports statuses until it is Succeeded, and then the result contains the extracted content and fields. Started and Queued mean the analysis is still in progress, and API keys and quota are never part of an analysis result.

q: Put the steps of an expense app that uses Content Understanding for receipts in the correct order. Not every step is used.
items: The app reads the total, date and merchant fields
The app generates a new receipt image
The employee uploads a photo of the receipt
The app creates the expense entry and sends low-confidence values for review
The app sends the photo to the receipt analyzer
exp: The employee uploads the receipt, the app analyzes it, reads the fields and then creates the expense entry, routing doubtful values to a reviewer. Generating a new receipt image would create content rather than capture the real expense.
